title: Desensitisation of neonatal rat pups for xenotransplantation with human tissues
protocol: Harvest mouse fetal tissue from E14 embryos.
Kill staged pregnant CD1 dams by cervical dislocation.
Remove the embryos by caesarian section.
Dissect the cortical brain tissue from the embryos.
Collect dissected cortical pieces in sterile high glucose DMEM/F12 medium.
Prepare dissociated cell suspensions for transplantation, desensitisation, or culture within 3 hours of donor sacrifice.
Collect human fetal tissue by donation within the MRC-sponsored South Wales Initiative for Fetal Tissue Transplantation (SWIFT) programme.
Ensure that tissue donation consent is obtained after approval and scheduling of termination of pregnancy procedures are completed.
Transport products of conception to the laboratory in sterile hibernation medium with added heparin for surgical procedures only.
Identify embryonic brain tissue.
Dissect cortical and striatal tissues.
Prepare dissociated cell suspensions for inoculation, grafting of primary fetal cells, or expansion of fetal neural progenitors.
Culture human cells as FNPs immediately after dissection.
Hibernate cells overnight in Hibernate E at 4°C for PF desensitisation or transplantation.
Prepare mouse and human PF tissues as dissociated cell suspensions by incubation in bovine trypsin at 4°C for 20 min.
Wash dissected tissue pieces in DMEM/F12.
Add bovine trypsin inhibitor and DNase to the wash solution.
Centrifuge the suspension for 3 min at 1000 rpm.
Resuspend the pellet in DMEM/F12.
Mechanically dissociate the tissue by trituration using a Gilson pipettor with yellow tips.
Determine cell numbers in suspension aliquots by trypan blue exclusion counting in a hemocytometer.
Prepare suspensions to a final concentration of 1 x 10^5 cells per μl for desensitisation or 2.5 x 10^5 cells per μl for grafting.
Incubate mouse-derived cells with a lacZ equine lentivirus under the CMV promoter for 20 min at a concentration of 7 x 10^8 i.u./ml, MOI = 2.
Centrifuge the cell suspension after incubation.
Resuspend cells at a final concentration of 1 or 2.5 x 10^5 cells/μl.
Transfer both human and mouse cells to the host within 3 h of preparation.
Dissect mouse and human striatal and cortical tissues for cell culture.
Incubate and dissociate tissues as described previously.
Dilute cells to a concentration of 200,000 cells/ml in B27 proliferation medium supplemented with growth factors.
Transfer diluted cells to sealed sterile filter-cap culture flasks.
Feed expanding populations of neurospheres by replacing half the medium every 4 days with fresh medium containing x2 concentration of supplements.
Resuspend the cells to a final concentration of 2.5 x 10^5 cells/μl in DMEM after 10 days in culture.
Cryostore cells at -80°C for thawing and transplantation approximately 10 weeks later.
Generate ES cell-derived neural precursors from the human ES cell line H9.
Add FGF-2 at a concentration of 20 ng/ml on day 8.
Add EGF at a concentration of 10 ng/ml on day 30.
Use ES cell-derived neural precursors for tolerising at day 30.
Prepare day 50 ES cell-derived neural precursor for transplantation.
Purchase pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats from a registered breeder.
House pregnant dams in individual cages until they give birth.
Wean pups at 28 days of age and sacrifice the mother by CO₂ overdose.
Sex the pups after weaning and house them in same-sex groups of 4-5 per cage.
Allow the rats to mature to adulthood for inclusion in transplantation experiments at 60-80 days of age.
Administer cyclosporin at a dose of 10 mg/kg daily starting one day prior to transplantation.
Separate pups briefly from the mother on the day of birth (P0).
Give an i.p. injection of 100,000 cells in 1 μl sterile DMEM using a handheld 10 μl SGE glass microsyringe with a 26 gauge needle.
Return the pups immediately to the mother after injection.
Handle the pups wearing disposable nitrile gloves to avoid risk of transfer of odours and potential rejection by the mother.
In individual experiments, some pups receive no tolerising injection.
Some pups receive similar injections on postnatal days 5 or 10 as above.
Some pups receive similar injections at 60 days of age once fully weaned.
Stereotaxically inject cells into the desensitised and control adult host rats' neostriatum.
Anaesthetise the rats with gaseous 1.5-3% isoflurane in a 2:1 O₂:NO mixture.
Mount the anaesthetised rats in a Kopf model 900 stereotaxic frame.
Expose the skull and drill a small burr hole over the right striatum.
Inject 500,000 human cells / 2 μl and 250,000 mouse cells / 2 μl via a 10 μl SGE glass microsyringe with removable wide bore needle and dome tip.

Target the injection at the right dorsal striatum, coordinates: anterior in front of bregma, AP = 0.6 mm; lateral to the midline, L = 2.6 mm; vertical below dura, V = -5.5 and -4.5 mm (1 μl at each depth).
Administer the injections over 2 min.
Allow a further 3 min for diffusion before slowly withdrawing the injection needle.
Clean the wound and suture.
Allow the animal to recover.
Give all animals a 5 ml injection subcutaneously of 5% glucose saline to avoid dehydration.
Administer paracetamol analgesia and tetracycline antibiotic via the water supply for 2 days following operation.
Sacrifice animals between 4 and 40 weeks after transplantation by barbiturate overdose (Euthatal, Merial Animal Health, Harlow, UK).
Perfuse the sacrificed animals via the ascending aorta with 50-100 ml of 0.1M phosphate buffered saline (PBS, pH=7.5) followed by 250-300 ml of 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS.
Remove brains and transfer to 20% sucrose until they sink.
Section brains at 40 μm thickness on a freezing sledge microtome.
Mount a 1:6 series of sections for cresyl violet staining.
Stain parallel free-floating series immunohistochemically using biotin-streptavidin kits with primary antibodies including β-galactosidase, human nuclear antigen (HuNu), DARPP-32, GABA, and GFAP.
Use Alexa Fluor 594 and 488 secondary antibodies for double immunofluorescence.
Dehydrate stained sections, mount, inspect, and photograph with a Leica DM-RBE microscope under bright field illumination.
Compute graft volumes and cell numbers by stereological measurement in an Olympus BX-50 microscope with motorised stage using CAST-GRID software.
Generate immunofluorescent images using the Leica TCS SP2 AOBS spectral confocal microscope.
Statistically evaluate cell survival using Analysis of Variance (ANOVA).
Undertake subsequent planned comparisons using Student’s t test for individual comparisons.
Apply Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons undertaken within the study.
Use restricted ANOVA to compare restricted sets of groups.
Apply Scheffé's S method to compare combinations of groups.
